(p-5943) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[1–2] ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened, and they said: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord."﴾ [al-Jinn: 1–2]

﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened﴾, i.e., to this wise Qur'an. It is well known that a nafar (group) ranges from three to ten, and it may be used for up to forty, like the rahṭ (company), as mentioned in al-Mujmal.

Al-Qashani said: It has already been explained that in existence there are earthly souls that are strong, not coarse like the predatory and bestial souls and their density and little perception, nor in the states and capacities of human souls, such that they would be bound to dense bodies, dominated by the earthly; nor in the purity and subtlety of the pure, detached souls, so as to connect with the higher world and be detached while attached to subtle elemental bodies, dominated by the airy, fiery or smoky, according to the variation of their states. Some philosophers called them the "suspended forms." They possess knowledge and perceptions of the same kind as ours. Since they are naturally close to the heavenly dominions, they are able to receive some of the unseen from their world, so it is not far-fetched that they ascend to the horizon of the heaven and steal hearing from the speech of the angels, i.e., the pure souls. And since they are earthly and weak in comparison with the heavenly powers, they are affected by the influence of those powers, and so their influence falls short of reaching their goal and grasping their extent of knowledge. It is not denied that their smoky bodies may be ignited by the rays of the stars and burn and perish, or be restrained from ascending to the heavenly horizon and be cast down. These are matters not outside the realm of possibility, and the truthful people of unveiling and direct witnessing have informed of them, from among the prophets and saints, especially the most perfect of them, our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. End.

(p-5944) As al-Qadi said, the verse indicates that he ﷺ did not see them and did not recite to them; rather, their presence coincided with some moments of his recitation, so they heard it, and Allah informed His Messenger of that.

﴿They said﴾, i.e., when they returned to their people, ﴿Indeed, we have heard a Qur'an﴾. Al-Mahayimi said: i.e., a book comprehensive of the divine and cosmic realities, the rulings and admonitions, and everything needed for the affairs of both abodes.

﴿Wondrous﴾ [al-Kahf: 63], i.e., strange, to which the expression of created beings is not suited, and which does not fall within their capacity. ﴿Guiding to right conduct﴾ [al-Jinn: 2], i.e., to the truth and the path of correctness. ﴿So we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord﴾ [al-Jinn: 2], i.e., of His creation, in worship alongside Him.

Remarks:

First: This situation resembles His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And when We turned towards you a group of the jinn listening to the Qur'an﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29], etc. Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with a group of his companions intending to go to the market of Ukaz." The devils had been prevented from receiving news of the heaven, and shooting stars were sent against them. So the devils returned and said: "What is wrong with you?" They said: "We have been prevented from receiving news of the heaven, and shooting stars have been sent against us!" He said: "Nothing has prevented you from receiving news of the heaven except something that has happened. So strike the eastern and western parts of the earth and see what this affair is that has happened." So they set out and struck the eastern and western parts of the earth, looking into what this affair was that had come between them and the news of the heaven. He said: Those who had headed toward Tihama went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Nakhla, while he was heading to the market of Ukaz and was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur'an, they listened to it and said: "This is what has come between you and the news of the heaven." Thereupon they returned to their people and said: "O our people! Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord." And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened﴾, and what was revealed to him was only the statement of the jinn. Muslim also narrated it, and added at its beginning: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ neither recited to the jinn nor saw them. He set out..." to its end.

Second: Al-Mawardi said: The apparent meaning of the verse is that they believed upon hearing the Qur'an. He said: Faith occurs in one of two ways: either by knowing the reality of the miraculous nature and the conditions of a miracle, so that he gains knowledge of the truthfulness of the Messenger; or by having knowledge from the earlier scriptures, in which there are indications that he is the prophet foretold. Both possibilities are conceivable for the jinn. End.

Third: Al-Razi said: In the verse there are several benefits:

One: that they should know thereby that he, peace be upon him, was sent to the jinn as he was sent to mankind.

Two: that the Quraysh should know that the jinn, despite their rebelliousness, when they heard the Qur'an, recognized its inimitability and believed in the Messenger.

Three: that the people should know that the jinn are accountable like humans.

Four: that it should be known that the jinn listen to our speech and understand our languages.

Five: that it should become clear that a believer among them calls others of his kind to faith.

In all these aspects there are many benefits if people come to know them. End.

When they heard the Qur'an and were granted success in monotheism and faith, they became aware of the error in what the disbelieving jinn had believed, namely likening Allah to His creation and taking for Him a consort and a son. So they magnified this and declared Him far above it, and they said:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 72, verse 3:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord, has not taken a companion or a son.﴾

﴿And that He, exalted is He, the majesty of our Lord, has not taken a companion or a son.﴾ That is: exalted is His dominion and His greatness, and the truth of His lordship, above taking a consort or a son.

(p-5946) Ibn Jarir said: al-jadd (majesty, fortune) here means al-hazz (portion, standing). It is said: "So-and-so has jadd in this matter" when he has a portion in it, and this is what is called in Persian al-bakht (fortune). The meaning is: His portion of dominion, sovereignty and great power is elevated, so there is no consort or son for Him, because a consort is only for the weak and incapable one, whom the driving desire compels to take her, and a son only comes from a desire that drives him to the intercourse from which a son results. So the group of jinn said: the dominion of our Lord, His sovereignty, His power and His greatness are too exalted to be weak with the weakness of His creation, who are compelled by desire to take a consort, or to have intercourse from which a child comes.

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[4–6] ﴿And that it was that our foolish one would say concerning Allah an excessive transgression﴾ ﴿And we thought that mankind and the jinn would never say a lie against Allah﴾ [al-Jinn: 5] ﴿And that it was that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, so they increased them in turmoil﴾ [al-Jinn: 6]

﴿And that it was that our foolish one would say﴾: by this they mean their misleader and seducer. ﴿concerning Allah an excessive transgression﴾: that is, a saying that exceeds all bounds. It is an attribute of a saying that is implied, with an omitted noun (muḍāf) understood. Or the very substance of "transgression" was made an intensification of it. Its origin (aṣl) is going beyond the limit, and what is meant by it is the attribution of a consort and offspring to Allah, exalted is He. ﴿And we thought that mankind and the jinn would never say a lie against Allah﴾ [al-Jinn: 5]: that is, in attributing to Him, glorified is He, what is not true. This is an excuse for their following the foolish one in that, since they thought that no one would lie against Allah, until the Qur'an made clear to them the lying and fabrication of the foolish one.

﴿And that it was that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, so they increased them in turmoil﴾ [al-Jinn: 6]. Ibn Jarir related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "In the Jahiliyyah, one of them would spend the night in the valley, and he would say: 'I seek refuge in the might of this valley,' and that increased them in sin."

So in the verse there is an allusion to what they believed in the Jahiliyyah (p-5947) that valleys are the abode of the jinn, and that their chieftains protect them from others. Likewise Ibrahim said: "When they descended into a valley they would say: 'We seek refuge in the lord of this valley from the evil of what is in it,' and the jinn would say: 'We do not possess for you nor for ourselves any harm or benefit.'"

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "They would say: 'So-and-so among the jinn is the lord of this valley,' and whenever one of them entered the valley he would seek refuge in the lord of the valley apart from Allah. He said: 'That would increase them in turmoil,' and turmoil is fear."

Ibn Zayd said: "A man in the Jahiliyyah, when he alighted in a valley before Islam, would say: 'I seek refuge in the greatest of this valley.' But when Islam came, they sought refuge in Allah and abandoned them." End of quotation.

That is: because that is shirk. For this reason the two surahs of seeking refuge (al-Mu'awwidhatan) were revealed, to teach seeking refuge in Allah alone, the Exalted, and disavowing seeking refuge in other than Him. Likewise the transmitted formulas of seeking refuge, for they serve as guidance to this.

Muslim related from Khawlah bint Hakim, who said: "Whoever alights at a place and says: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created,' nothing will harm him until he departs from that place."

Some of them said: In the hadith is an explanation of the verse about the jinn, and that what is in it is shirk, and that the fact that a thing brings a worldly benefit, by warding off an evil or bringing about a gain, does not indicate that it is not shirk.

There is a strange interpretation of the verse, transmitted by al-Razi, namely that what is meant is: there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among mankind also, but from the evil of the jinn, such as a man saying: "I seek refuge in the Messenger of Allah from the evil of the jinn of this valley." The proponents of this interpretation were led to it only because "rajul" (man) is a name for a human and not a name for a jinn. This is weak, for no proof has been established that a male jinn is not called a "rajul." End of quotation.

The pronoun in ﴿so they increased them﴾ [al-Jinn: 6] refers to the jinn, in the sense: they increased them, by their seeking refuge with them, in error, sin and misguidance. Or it refers to mankind, in the sense: they increased the jinn, by their seeking refuge, in arrogance and insolence.

And (al-Rahaq), in its origin, is the overtaking of a thing, so it was specified for what befalls one of pride or misguidance.

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 72, verses 7–9:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7–9] ﴿And that they thought, as you thought, that Allah would never resurrect anyone.﴾ ﴿And that we touched the heaven and found it filled with a strong guard and meteors.﴾ [al-Jinn: 8] ﴿And that we used to sit in it on [certain] seats for listening. But whoever listens now will find for himself a watching meteor.﴾ [al-Jinn: 9]

﴿And that they﴾ means: and it was revealed to me that the jinn ﴿thought, as you thought﴾, that is, in your jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam).

﴿That Allah would never resurrect anyone﴾ means: a messenger to His creation, calling them to His tawhid (monotheism) and to that which is their happiness. Or: that Allah would never raise anyone from his grave for reckoning and recompense.

It has been said: the pronoun in "and that they" refers to mankind, going with the view that His saying ﴿And that there were men﴾ [al-Jinn: 6] and ﴿And that they thought﴾ are part of the speech of the jinn, and the address is to them.

﴿And that we touched the heaven﴾ [al-Jinn: 8] means: we sought to reach the heaven and to listen to the speech of its inhabitants. ﴿And found it filled with a strong guard and meteors﴾ [al-Jinn: 8] means: guardians and projectiles.

﴿And that we used to sit in it on [certain] seats for listening. But whoever listens now will find for himself a watching meteor﴾ [al-Jinn: 9] means: we used to sit in the heaven on seats in order to listen to what happens and what will occur in it. But whoever listens now will find for himself a flame of fire that has been set in watch for him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: In His saying ﴿filled﴾ [al-Jinn: 8] there is evidence that what has occurred is the filling and the abundance. Likewise His saying ﴿we used to sit in it on seats﴾ [al-Jinn: 9] means: we used to find some of the seats empty of guards and meteors, but now all the seats are filled. This is a mention of what drove them to travel through the lands until they came upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and listened to his recitation.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[20–21] ﴿Say: Indeed, I only call upon my Lord, and I associate none with Him.﴾ ﴿Say: Indeed, I do not possess for you any harm or any right guidance.﴾ [al-Jinn: 21]

﴿Say﴾ (and it is read as "He said"): ﴿Indeed, I only call upon my Lord﴾, i.e., I worship Him and supplicate to Him alone. ﴿And I associate none with Him﴾, i.e., this is no novelty or outrageous matter that should cause your astonishment or your unanimous hostility toward me.

﴿Say: Indeed, I do not possess for you any harm or any right guidance﴾ [al-Jinn: 21], i.e., because that belongs to Allah Exalted alone, so do not hasten me toward the punishment.

Al-Shihab, in clarifying what al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) said here, stated: Either "right guidance" is meant as benefit, expressing the name of the cause for the effect, or "harm" is meant as misguidance, expressing the name of the effect for the cause. It is also permissible that each of them be stripped of what is mentioned in the other, making it an ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which each of two contrasted terms is omitted from one clause and mentioned in the other). The estimated meaning is: "I do not possess for you any harm or any benefit, nor any misguidance or right guidance."

A note of clarification:

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is that none attains knowledge of the unseen except the one who is chosen, who is specifically the chosen one for prophethood, not every person who is approved.

He said: In this there is a refutation of the miracles of saints (karamat), because those who are attributed to them, even if they are approved saints, are not messengers. God has singled out the messengers from among the approved ones with knowledge of the unseen, and with the refutation of soothsaying and astrology, because their practitioners are the farthest of all things from being approved and the most deserving of wrath. End of quotation.

Abu al-Su'ud answered that the meaning of the verse is: He does not reveal His unseen to anyone of His creation with a complete disclosure by which the clear state of affairs is unveiled with a perfect unveiling that produces the certainty of direct sight, ﴿except to a messenger whom He has chosen﴾ [Al-Jinn: 27]. That is: except a messenger whom He has chosen to reveal to him some of His hidden matters that are connected with his message, as the explanation of ﴿whom He has chosen﴾ [Al-Jinn: 27] with "messenger" indicates, a complete connection. This is either because they are among the foundations of his message, such as a miracle indicating its truth, or because they are among its rulings and principles, like the general legal obligations imposed upon those who are responsible, the manners of their deeds, the recompense that follows them in the Hereafter, and the conditions of the Hereafter on which those obligations depend, among which is the Hour and the resurrection, and other unseen matters whose explanation is among the functions of the message. As for what is not connected with it in either of these two ways, from among the unseen matters, among which is the establishment of the Hour, He does not reveal it to anyone ever. Moreover, stating its time would disrupt the legislative wisdom upon which the orbit of the message revolves. There is nothing in this that indicates the negation of the miracles of the saints connected with unveiling. For the restriction of the farthest stage of unveiling to the messengers does not require that no level of those stages be attained by others at all, nor does anyone claim for any of the saints what is in the rank of the messengers, peace be upon them, of complete unveiling attained through explicit revelation. End of quotation.

Its summary is restricting the unseen to what is a miracle or among the functions of the message. Al-Nasafi also followed this line in the answer, with an indication of the distinction. His wording is: That is: except a messenger whom He has chosen for knowledge of some of the unseen, so that his report of the unseen may be a miracle for him, for He reveals to him of His unseen whatever He wills. And "from a messenger" [Al-Jinn: 27] is an explanation of "whom He has chosen" [Al-Jinn: 27]. The saint, when he reports something and it happens, is not certain about it, but he reports based on a dream or on insight. Moreover, every miracle of a saint is a miracle of the messenger. End of quotation.

Al-Razi said: In my view, the verse contains no indication of anything they have said, meaning al-Zamakhshari and those who followed him. What it indicates is that His words "His unseen" [Al-Jinn: 26] contain no form of generality, so it suffices in acting upon its requirement that He not reveal to His creation any single one of His unseen matters. We therefore take it to refer to the time of the occurrence of the Hour, [p-5955] so the meaning of the verse is that He does not reveal this unseen to anyone, and there remains in the verse no indication that He does not reveal any of the unseen matters to anyone.

He said: What confirms this interpretation is that He mentioned this verse directly after His words:

﴿"I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will set for it a long term."﴾ meaning: I do not know the time of the occurrence of the Hour. Then He said after it: ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not reveal His unseen to anyone﴾ [Al-Jinn: 26], that is: the time of the occurrence of the Hour, from the unseen that God does not reveal to anyone. In sum, His words "His unseen" [Al-Jinn: 26] is a singular noun in construct form, so it suffices in acting upon it to take it as one unseen matter. As for generality, there is no indication of it in the wording.

If it is said: If you interpret that as the Hour, then how does He say ﴿except to a messenger whom He has chosen﴾ [Al-Jinn: 27], when He does not reveal this unseen to any of His messengers?

We say: Rather, He reveals it as the Hour draws near, and how could it not be, when He says: ﴿And on the day the sky is split open with clouds, and the angels are sent down in descent﴾ [Al-Furqan: 25]. Without doubt, the angels at that time know that the Hour is established. Also, it is possible that this exception is disjunctive, as if He said: "He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not reveal His particular unseen, which is the Day of Resurrection, to anyone." Then He said after it: "But whomever of the messengers He has chosen, He sends before him and behind him guards who protect him from the evil of the rebellious among humankind and jinn," because He mentioned this statement only as an answer to the question of one who asked about the time of the occurrence of the Hour in mockery, and in contempt of his religion and his message. In sum, His words restrict the unseen to the time of the occurrence of the Hour by the indication of the context, and the messenger to the angel. End of quotation.

In "al-'Inayah" he disputed this, saying that the acceptable reading is to take "messenger" in its common sense, because the context and the flow of the discourse indicate this. Al-Nasafi transmitted from al-Ta'wilat something of this kind:

Some of them said: In this verse is a refutation of the astrologers (munajjimah). But this is not the case, for among them are some whose reports are believed, and likewise the physicians (mutatabbibah), who know the natures of plants, which cannot be known by mere reflection. So it is known that they gained their knowledge from a messenger whose trace has ended, while his knowledge remained among creation. End of quotation.

This answer is one that the jurists (mutafaqqihah) resort to, claiming that knowing the times of eclipses and the special properties of simple substances [p-5956] is among what is included in the knowledge of the unseen. The correct view is that it does not include such matters, because they are among what people can readily come to know through observation, reasoning, experimentation and research, like the mathematical sciences, the natural sciences, agriculture, the crafts, and astronomy.

In sum, whatever a human can attain by himself is not part of the unseen at all. For this reason some of the wise said: If it were among the function of the Prophet to explain the natural and astronomical sciences, then the faculties of sense and intellect would have to be disabled, independence would be removed from humankind, and every individual would be obliged to accept everything on trust. The number of messengers in each nation would have to be sufficient to teach its members, at every time, all that they need for the affairs of their livelihood and their hereafter. Or, if you wish, say: it would have to be that the human would not be this kind of being that we know. Yes, the prophets alert people in general terms to the use of their senses and intellects in everything that increases their benefits and their knowledge by which their souls are elevated, but while linking this with pointing out what strengthens faith and increases reflection. The Prophet ﷺ has already guided us to the obligation of our independence from him in the affairs of our worldly life, in the incident of pollinating palm trees, when he said: "You are more knowledgeable about the affairs of your worldly life." End of quotation. So keep this in mind, for it is among what is precious and should not be entrusted to those who are not its people.

A note of clarification:

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is that none attains knowledge of the unseen except the one who is chosen, who is specifically the chosen one for prophethood, not every person who is approved.

He said: In this there is a refutation of the miracles of saints (karamat), because those who are attributed to them, even if they are approved saints, are not messengers. God has singled out the messengers from among the approved ones with knowledge of the unseen, and with the refutation of soothsaying and astrology, because their practitioners are the farthest of all things from being approved and the most deserving of wrath. End of quotation.

Abu al-Su'ud answered that the meaning of the verse is: He does not reveal His unseen to anyone of His creation with a complete disclosure by which the clear state of affairs is unveiled with a perfect unveiling that produces the certainty of direct sight, ﴿except to a messenger whom He has chosen﴾ [Al-Jinn: 27]. That is: except a messenger whom He has chosen to reveal to him some of His hidden matters that are connected with his message, as the explanation of ﴿whom He has chosen﴾ [Al-Jinn: 27] with "messenger" indicates, a complete connection. This is either because they are among the foundations of his message, such as a miracle indicating its truth, or because they are among its rulings and principles, like the general legal obligations imposed upon those who are responsible, the manners of their deeds, the recompense that follows them in the Hereafter, and the conditions of the Hereafter on which those obligations depend, among which is the Hour and the resurrection, and other unseen matters whose explanation is among the functions of the message. As for what is not connected with it in either of these two ways, from among the unseen matters, among which is the establishment of the Hour, He does not reveal it to anyone ever. Moreover, stating its time would disrupt the legislative wisdom upon which the orbit of the message revolves. There is nothing in this that indicates the negation of the miracles of the saints connected with unveiling. For the restriction of the farthest stage of unveiling to the messengers does not require that no level of those stages be attained by others at all, nor does anyone claim for any of the saints what is in the rank of the messengers, peace be upon them, of complete unveiling attained through explicit revelation. End of quotation.

Its summary is restricting the unseen to what is a miracle or among the functions of the message. Al-Nasafi also followed this line in the answer, with an indication of the distinction. His wording is: That is: except a messenger whom He has chosen for knowledge of some of the unseen, so that his report of the unseen may be a miracle for him, for He reveals to him of His unseen whatever He wills. The saint, when he reports something and it happens, is not certain about it, but he reports based on a dream or on insight. Moreover, every miracle of a saint is a miracle of the messenger. End of quotation.

What it indicates is that His words "His unseen" [Al-Jinn: 26] contain no form of generality, so it suffices in acting upon its requirement that He not reveal to His creation any single one of His unseen matters. We therefore take it to refer to the time of the occurrence of the Hour, [p-5955] so the meaning of the verse is that He does not reveal this unseen to anyone, and there remains in the verse no indication that He does not reveal any of the unseen matters to anyone.

He said: What confirms this interpretation is that He mentioned this verse directly after His words:

﴿"I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will set for it a long term."﴾ meaning: I do not know the time of the occurrence of the Hour. Some of them said: In this verse is a refutation of the astrologers (munajjimah). Or, if you wish, say: it would have to be that the human would not be this kind of being that we know. Yes, the prophets alert people in general terms to the use of their senses and intellects in everything that increases their benefits and their knowledge by which their souls are elevated, but while linking this with pointing out what strengthens faith and increases reflection. The Prophet ﷺ has already guided us to the obligation of our independence from him in the affairs of our worldly life, in the incident of pollinating palm trees, when he said: "You are more knowledgeable about the affairs of your worldly life." End of quotation. So keep this in mind, for it is among what is precious and should not be entrusted to those who are not its people.

And His words, Exalted is He:

The commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿That He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord. And He encompasses what is with them, and He has enumerated everything in number.﴾

﴿That He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾ is connected to ﴿He makes [a guard] proceed﴾ [al-Jinn: 27], as a purpose clause (ghayah) for it. The pronoun [in "they"] refers either to the "guards" (al-Rasad), or to ﴿whom He has approved﴾ [al-Jinn: 27], and the plural is in consideration of the meaning of "min" (whoever), i.e., "that they may convey," so that the object of His knowledge becomes manifest. The mention of His knowledge here is for the sake of attending to the matter of conveying, for alerting to the consequence of reward being based upon it, for emphasizing the exhortation to it, and for warning against neglecting it.

﴿And He encompasses what is with them﴾ means: with what is with the guards (al-Rasad), or with the Messengers, peace be upon them. It is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of ﴿He makes [a guard] proceed﴾ [al-Jinn: 27], brought in order to affirm His self-sufficiency in knowledge of the conveying, apart from what was mentioned of the guards' passage.

﴿And He has enumerated everything in number﴾ means: one by one, owing to the breadth of His knowledge. It is a second affirmation of His encompassing what is with the Messengers of His revelation and speech, and of promise and threat, as is known from its parallels.
